item.title: Apple Seeks Preliminary Injunction Against OpenAI in Trade Secrets Case
item.description: judge for a preliminary injunction barring two former employees and OpenAI from accessing, acquiring, using or disclosing alleged confidential information as it moves ahead with its trade secrets case. “Apple’s request for a preliminary injunction is both based on false information and completely unnecessary because we do not have, nor want, any of their trade secrets,” OpenAI said in a blogpost late on Monday. Apple last month sued OpenAI and the two former employees, both now working for OpenAI, alleging misappropriation of its trade secrets to benefit the ChatGPT-owner’s foray into consumer hardware, a dramatic escalation of already simmering tension between the two companies.

item.title: NHTSA: Some Older Ford Cars, SUVs Pose Unreasonable Safety Risks
item.description: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said on Monday that some older Ford cars and SUVs pose unreasonable safety risks because the timing belt may fail and cause them to lose power or engines to seize. “Based on NHTSA’s analysis of the data, failure rates, information provided by Ford, preliminary engine teardown analysis, and precedent recalls regarding loss of engine oil pressure with the presence of driver facing warnings, (the agency) believes there is an unreasonable risk to motor vehicle safety,” NHTSA said. auto safety regulator upgraded a defect investigation into about 135,000 Ford Fiesta, Ford Focus and Ford EcoSport vehicles with 1.0L engines from various model years between 2014 and 2021.

item.title: UN, Scientists Warn Strong El Niño Will Add Fuel to ‘Planet Already on Fire’
item.description: A strengthening El Niño has already broken records for intensity at its early stages, and it is likely to spark even more wild weather worldwide as it grows, “adding fuel to a planet already on fire,” United Nations officials warned Friday. “We have already endured a summer of extremes — record-shattering heat domes; apocalyptic wildfires raging in Spain, France and far beyond; thousands of lives lost in the scorching conditions.” “But according to the latest science, this is only a warm-up act,” Guterres said, indicating that as El Niño strengthens, it will be “adding fuel to a planet already on fire.” “We are in uncharted territory,” he said. A key area of the Pacific Ocean used to measure the strength of El Niño reached its warmest and most intense level ever recorded for the 15th week since it formed, which is early in its lifetime, scientists at Columbia University reported.

item.title: Europe’s Wildfire Season Exposes Climate Insurance Gap
item.description: Domestic insurers are expected to absorb most of the losses from Europe’s worst wildfire season in recent history, but the blazes are also raising a bigger question: who will pay as climate-driven disasters become more frequent and destructive? Fires have also swept through Spain and Greece, fueling concerns about rising insurance costs and widening gaps in protection against climate-related risks. “This might be a real threat to the industry if you have a wildfire out of control, reaching a medium-sized city like Bordeaux,” said Marcos Alvarez, managing director at Morningstar DBRS.

item.title: California Sees 25% Decline in Vehicle Thefts in 2025
item.description: California recorded its second consecutive year of declining vehicle thefts in 2025, according to newly released data by the California Highway Patrol (CHP). The decline in vehicle thefts began in 2024, when California recorded its first year-over-year decrease since 2019. On average, a vehicle was stolen in California about every four minutes in 2025.

Jessica’s appointment strengthens our ability to deliver industry-specific risk expertise as the sector continues to innovate and expand to meet growing demand for AI compute capacity.” Fields added, “I’m thrilled to join Marsh at such a critical time for the technology industry. item.title: Ageas Re unveils regional organisation to strengthen client proximity
item.description: Brussels headquartered reinsurer Ageas Re will adopt a regional organisation structure from September 1st, 2026, a move designed to optimise client proximity and accessibility to its services, Chief Executive Officer (CEO), Joachim Racz, announced today. The new, more client focused organisation at Ageas Re includes the regions EMEA P&C, Americas P&C, and International & Specialty, which will sit alongside the company’s Products & Practices division. “As we go into a challenging renewal season with a new organization, the teams will ensure a seamless transition to further strengthen client and partner services.

item.title: Domtar A.W. Resolves Clean Air Act Violations with $1.5M Civil Penalty
item.description: The Justice Department has resolved alleged Clean Air Act and Arkansas Water and Air Pollution Control Act violations with Domtar A.W., a manufacturer of pulps, paper and wood products. Under the proposed consent decree, Domtar will pay a $1.5 million civil penalty, divided between the United States and the state of Arkansas. This settlement resolves Domtar’s failure to follow federal and state requirements to capture and control air emissions from its brown stock washer.

item.title: Kansas Launches Program for First Responders Recovering from Trauma
item.description: The Helping First Responders Overcoming Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder, or HERO Act, is a pilot program to help emergency responders by providing reimbursement for assessment and treatment of certain psychological conditions resulting from duty-related trauma. A million dollars is set aside to be administered through the pilot program to eligible first responders. First responders who meet the requirements may be eligible to receive reimbursement for the diagnosis and treatment of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), acute stress disorder (ASD), or subclinical syndromes of either disorder as a direct result of a duty-related traumatic event.

item.title: Texas AG Investigates Major Food Manufacturers for Misleading “Heart-Healthy” Labeling
item.description: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton announced an investigation into major food manufacturers that market their products as “heart-healthy,” alleging that many companies have adopted such labels on products that are high in added sugars, refined grains and inflammatory properties. As part of the investigation, Attorney General Paxton has issued Civil Investigative Demands (“CIDs”) to food manufacturers that use the “heart-healthy” label. “I won’t allow corporations to slap a ‘heart healthy’ symbol on their food labels as an attempt to market seed oils and other chemical-filled foods as healthy,” said Paxton.

item.title: INTX launches native AI intelligence layer across (re)insurance operating platform
item.description: The post INTX launches native AI intelligence layer across (re)insurance operating platform appeared first on Insurtech Insights . INTX Insurance Software has launched Tenet , which it describes as the insurance industry’s first native intelligence layer embedded directly into a unified (re)insurance operating system, as insurers increasingly look to move beyond standalone AI assistants toward enterprise-wide decision support. According to INTX, the platform operates across its ReinsureConnect ceded reinsurance platform, INTX Re assumed reinsurance platform and INTX Core commercial P&C system, creating a single intelligence layer across underwriting, reinsurance, claims and financial operations.

item.title: Trucordia acquires Shipley & Pease Insurance
item.description: Trucordia has acquired the assets of Shipley & Pease Insurance, a brokerage specializing in professional liability insurance and risk management services for architects and engineers. Founded in 1996 by Dave Shipley and later expanded under Stan Pease, Shipley & Pease has grown into one of the largest independently owned brokerages focused on the architects and engineers market. The firm said it has grown 500% over the past decade, driven primarily by client referrals, and is a founding member of AE ProNet, a network of brokers, insurers, and attorneys focused on insurance and risk management solutions for the design industry.

item.title: UNest adds Ladder life insurance offering
item.description: UNest, a college savings platform for families, now promotes Ladder within its app, allowing users to obtain a term life insurance quote as part of the experience. The company previously partnered with Haven Life, offering members a $5 contribution to a child’s UNest savings account for requesting a term life insurance quote, while existing Haven Life policyholders received a $25 investment into their UNest account. UNest has also worked with Avibra and Wysh to bring insurance-related offerings to its users.

item.title: HappyRobot raises $150 million
item.description: HappyRobot, a company building “enterprise superintelligence,” has raised $150 million in Series C funding led by Prysm Capital and co-led by Eurazeo. The round values the company at $1.2 billion post-money, bringing total funding to around $200 million. After first “proving” its platform in logistics, HappyRobot is expanding across the supply chain as well as into insurance, energy and utilities, telecommunications, airlines, and other sectors where business-critical work still depends on manual coordination across fragmented systems.

item.title: Where Private Investigation Firms and Claims Professionals Intersect
item.description: The most effective private investigation firms intentionally build teams that understand both sides of the claims process. View Series Prior to joining the private investigation industry, I spent nine years working in insurance claims handling and Special Investigations Unit (SIU) roles. Although claims professionals and private investigators work for different organizations, we ultimately share the same objective.

item.title: The Takeaway: Go to Where the Problem Lives
item.description: The trucking project described in the accompanying article, “ Design the Team Before You Design the Solution: Commercial Trucking Case Study ,” succeeded when a team shifted its perspective on whose problem it was solving. Here’s how to build the learnings captured by the case study into how you and your team approach your next complex problem. Before bringing in outside perspectives, write down your current working theory of the problem.

item.title: Design the Team Before You Design the Solution: Commercial Trucking Case Study
item.description: Below the article, Bassett summarizes takeaways from the case study, providing a How-To guide to help readers design the teams they need to solve their next complex problems. For readers interested in a tear sheet, the takeaways are also published separately in the linked article, " Go to Where the Problem Lives ." Carrier Management previously published an article about how to address the problem of strategic drift that can stall innovation teams, " Reframing Like a Fox: How Insurance Leaders Can Catch Strategic Drift Before It Compounds ." In this article, we explore an insurance case study that illustrates how understanding the way that we individually interpret a problem—shaped by how we perceive our environment—is key to assembling teams that can see a challenge both in its parts and as a whole. One topic that we returned to repeatedly was small commercial trucking fleets—logistics firms with fewer than 16 cabs that had often grown from owner-operator arrangements into complex businesses that required real management oversight.

Also, that she had failed to take proper care when giving pension transfer advice. item.title: A Record 14 Billion-Dollar Rounds In July Pushed Venture’s Historic Run Higher
item.description: Startup capital totaled $65 billion, up 100% year over year, as the month notched the highest-ever number of billion-dollar venture rounds on record, per Crunchbase data. Fourteen startups raised billion-dollar rounds in July, the highest count in a single month, though not the largest amount raised in such deals, an analysis of Crunchbase data shows. July ranked as the third-largest funding month of the year, up 10% over June, following on the heels of a record-breaking first half of 2026 , when startups raised $515 billion globally.

item.title: TWIA renewal came in almost 12% under budget. Staff to recommend Gallagher Re continue
item.description: The Texas Windstorm Insurance Association’s (TWIA) reinsurance and catastrophe bond renewal for 2026 came in almost 12% under its budgeted spend for the coverage, while at a meeting later today its staff will recommend it continues with Gallagher Re as its reinsurance broker. The net cost of TWIA’s 2026 reinsurance program came out at $199.4 million, which is almost 12% under the budgeted amount of $225.2 million. TWIA’s staff will explain that, “The favorable budget variance is a result of the PML being set slightly below the initial estimate incorporated into the budget as well as a softening of the global reinsurance market, resulting in lower reinsurance costs overall.” On a rate-on-line (ROL) basis, it seems TWIA’s program came in around 10% down on the prior year, with an overall ROL for the 2026 reinsurance tower of 9.21%, compared to 10.2% a year earlier.

item.title: Aon promotes Murray to Global Chief Commercial Officer, Captive & Insurance Management
item.description: Aon has promoted long-standing Bermuda based employee Choisel Murray to a senior position as Global Chief Commercial Officer within the Aon Captive & Insurance Management business. Prior to her recent promotion to Global Chief Commercial Officer, Murray was a Deputy Managing Director in Aon’s Captive & Insurance Management division, also with responsibilities in Commercial Risk Solutions. As a result, with insurance management activities sitting within this business unit of the global insurance and reinsurance broker, as well as the captive commercial leadership, Murray will also be the global commercial leader on activities across special purpose insurer (SPI), segregated and protected account structures, which are often utilised to facilitate insurance-linked securities (ILS) arrangements, transform risks to transfer them to the capital markets, and can be issuance vehicles for ILS instruments including catastrophe bonds.

item.title: Talcott launches West Grove Re life and annuity sidecar with $1bn capital raise
item.description: International life and annuity insurance specialist Talcott Financial Group (Talcott) has announced the launch of West Grove Re Ltd., a Bermuda based reinsurance sidecar structure that has been capitalised with approximately $1 billion after a fund-raise in partnership with Goldman Sachs. The roughly $1 billion capital raise for West Grove Re includes equity commitments from Talcott, Goldman Sachs Asset & Wealth Management (AWM) and its clients, as well as a credit facility, Talcott further explained. Talcott becomes the latest major life and annuity player to launch a reinsurance sidecar, to bring third-party capital to support its business.

item.title: Ceres supports California proposal on long-term insurance solvency planning
item.description: In a comment letter submitted to the California Department of Insurance, Ceres said the proposed Long-Term Solvency Planning Regulation would strengthen oversight of the state’s insurance sector while bringing it into line with solvency and transition-planning approaches already adopted by regulators in other parts of the world. Ceres, a US-based non-profit organisation that works with investors, companies and policymakers to advance sustainable business practices and improve the management of climate-related financial risks, has voiced its support for a proposed California regulation that would require the state’s largest domestic insurers to prepare long-term solvency plans addressing financial risks, including those linked to extreme weather. Commenting on the proposal, Steven Rothstein, Chief Programme Officer at Ceres, said the regulation would provide “much needed visibility into how carriers are preparing for future risk.” He added that California’s residents, communities and businesses needed “an insurance market capable of weathering the climate and technology challenges ahead,” describing the proposed framework as an important step towards building that resilience.

item.title: Lockton expands availability of AI-enabled intelligence platform across US business
item.description: Lockton, a privately held insurance brokerage and risk management firm, has announced that its Lockton SAGE enterprise intelligence platform is now being made available more widely across its US business. The platform has been developed to combine Lockton’s proprietary data, advanced analytics, AI-enabled technology and specialist knowledge to help clients make more informed decisions. Originally launched within Lockton Re, Lockton SAGE is now being expanded across Lockton’s wider US operations, including Risk Solutions, People Solutions and Reinsurance, according to the firm.

item.title: NYC Mayor Mamdani’s Rent Freeze Heaps Pressure on a Teetering CMBS Deal
item.description: Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s rent freeze threatens to make it worse. The deal has become a closely watched barometer of the investability of rent-stabilized housing sectors in New York and, increasingly, nationwide as more cities tighten or consider rent controls . Market watchers say the looming freeze — a central promise of Mamdani’s campaign that launched him into City Hall — will further erode recoveries and discourage capital from flowing into the sector.

item.description: It also sets out how CEOs should think about AI as a strategic capability, including where it may change operating models, decision rights, talent requirements and the way specialist insurance businesses compete.  Key findings from the report include:  AI advantage in commercial and specialty reinsurance is likely to compound where it improves judgement on complex risks and portfolios CEOs need to look beyond productivity use cases and decide where AI changes the organisation’s shape, motion and direction Leadership teams should assess whether they have the operating model, governance and data foundations to scale AI responsibly The firms that move fastest may not be those with the most pilots, but those that make AI part of how strategic and underwriting decisions are made The post Oxbow Partners launches CEO Agenda for AI in commercial and specialty (re)insurance appeared first on Insurtech Insights . item.title: Orion180 expands private flood insurance to California

item.title: Lockton Re executes ILW covering property cat and cyber risks in a single limit
item.description: Reinsurance broker Lockton Re has successfully executed what the firm believes is the first industry-loss warranty (ILW) that combines property catastrophe and cyber risk triggers within a single limit structure for a protection buying client. Lockton Re explained that this demonstrates how the industry-loss warranty (ILW) market can continued to evolve beyond traditional property-only use-cases, while further underscoring the increasing maturity of the cyber ILW and industry-loss index trigger sector. As the ILW market continues to evolve, we are seeing broader demand from clients for risk solutions that look at new structures and integrated options, and we are particularly excited about the opportunity for growth in this space with more bespoke, alternative index covers for our clients.” Theo Norris, International ILS and Cyber ILS Leader, Lockton Re Capital Markets, further stated, “This deal highlights trends we are seeing with the convergence of property catastrophe and cyber risk transfer, the growing maturity of industry cyber loss indices, and the development of new capital solutions for the market.

item.title: Bowhead Specialty’s H1’26 net income jumps 35% on premium growth and underwriting profitability
item.description: Bowhead Specialty has reported H1 2026 net income of $32.1 million, up 35.3% from $23.8 million in the same period of 2025, as the specialty insurer continued to grow premiums while maintaining an underwriting profit. At the same time, Bowhead’s net investment income rose 40.4% to $36.8 million in H1 2026, and its underwriting profitability remained intact, with the combined ratio improving to 95.6% from 96.9% in H1 2025. In Q2 2026 alone, Bowhead reported net income of $16.1 million, up 30.8% from $12.3 million in H1 2025, while adjusted net income increased 26.5% to $16.1 million.

item.title: Spokane wildfires burn 7,000 acres, destroy 700 structures as Guy Carpenter warns of continued spread

Guy Carpenter continued, “Above-normal significant wildfire potential persists across much of the West, with additional hotspots in the southern Plains and Florida during August.

item.title: New Jersey Settles Trucker Misclassification Claims for $2.7 Million
item.description: The New Jersey Department of Labor and Workforce Development (NJDOL) has reached a $2.7 million settlement with STG Logistics, Inc. This settlement resolves the first lawsuit filed under New Jersey’s 2021 law that permits the state to file suit in New Jersey Superior Court against employers who have misclassified workers as independent contractors. STG Logistics purchased XPO’s New Jersey intermodal business in 2022 and assumed liability for the its past employment practices.
